content: Abdominal or pelvic fullness, flushing (commonly referred to as hot flashes), breast tenderness, headache, or dizziness may occur as side effects of this medication. It is important to understand that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the potential benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. During treatment with clomiphene, vision changes such as blurred vision, seeing spots, or flashes of light may sometimes occur, particularly when exposed to bright light. These visual disturbances typically resolve within a few days or weeks after discontinuing the medication. However, in rare cases, these changes in vision may become permanent. This medication may also lead to a condition known as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). In rare instances, severe OHSS can cause a sudden accumulation of fluid in the abdomen, chest, and heart area. This condition may develop during therapy or after the treatment has been stopped. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking clomiphene, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. The use of clomiphene may increase the likelihood of multiple births, such as twins or triplets. This medication may also cause dizziness or vision changes. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness or clear vision until you are certain you can perform them safely. Limit your consumption of alcoholic beverages. Discontinue this medication as soon as you become pregnant, as it must not be used during pregnancy. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk, but it may reduce milk production. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as hormone levels, pelvic examinations, or ultrasounds) should be conducted as directed. Ensure that you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor promptly for further instructions. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in June 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
